text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Belgium's Deputy Prime Minister Philippe Maystadt spent the second day of his four-day trade mission to Vietnam in talks with ministries and told Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong that Belgium would provide a $17 million grant to Vietnam for 1996-98.
-- The building and construction of 19 bridges on a section of National 1 between Ho Chi Minh City and Can Tho in the Mekong Delta is due to start here today.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has signed a protocol to merge the Vietnam Geological Department and the Mineral Resources Management Department into the Geology and Mineral Resources Department.
-- A 24-year-old Vietnamese woman who works for the weekly Vietnam Investment Review has been chosen to participate in an international South Pole exploration team.
-- The politburo has asked all Communist Party cells to reinforce their activities aimed at combatting drug abuse.
-- Vietnam has exported 40,000 tonnes of coffee from the 1996/1997 crop so far and expects a total output of 250,000 tonnes.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai was told that the Asian Development Bank will give Vietnam a loan of $300-350 million each year. The paper did not specify over how many years these loans would continue. The ADB has received a licence to set up a representative office in the country in January.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for improvement of the country's health care system.
-- A U.S trade delegation arrived in Hanoi on Sunday to continue discussions on a trade treaty between the two countries.

-- The Hanoi Police has issued orders for the arrest of a lieutenant-colonel of the Interior Ministry's Investigation Police Department on suspicion of involvement in a drug trafficking case, bringing the number of people arrested in the probe to 26.
